messages:
maya: Heads-up: ACME Prod (private deployment) says all console graphs for their tenant dropped to zero around 02:15 UTC after we rolled the auth-proxy config. They can still call the API and get responses, but usage/latency charts are empty. :worried:
ian: :eyes: can you paste an example request from the runtime logs? Do we see tenant headers coming through?
maya: Logs show requests hitting redwood-runtime and auth successful. Example from runtime access log:
```
ts=2025-11-01T02:16:04Z method=POST path=/v1/generate status=200 tenant_header="-" remote_ip=10.0.12.8
```
Note tenant_header is `-` which is wrong (should be the tenant id).
ashok: Oof. Sounds like header mangled somewhere. Which header name does ACME expect? X-Acme-Tenant?
maya: They use `X-Tenant-ID` previously. Our telemetry pipeline expects `x-tenant-id` (lowercase) and the console maps tenants by that header value.
jonathan: We recently normalized header names in the auth-proxy (to avoid duplicates). There's a new setting `preserve_original_header_case: false` in the release notes. If it drops the header when an Authorization header exists, that could explain it.
ian: Reproducer: curl to the customer gateway with tenant header included returns ok, but runtime logs show the header missing. Quick reproduce command I ran from inside customer VPC:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Tenant-ID: acme-42" https://private-gw.acme.example/v1/generate
```
Response 200, but runtime access log shows tenant header empty.
maya: Support ticket also included a screenshot of console with all charts zero and the tenant filter dropdown showing acme-42 but zero datapoints.
ashok: Hypothesis: auth-proxy normalization rewrites `X-Tenant-ID` to `x-tenant-id`, then an upstream rewrite step inside the private gateway strips unknown headers unless explicitly allowed. Another angle: the proxy rotates OIDC and uses a sanitized header map and drops anything that conflicts with internal claim names.
jonathan: I pulled the auth-proxy config from the rollout: we set `strip_untrusted_headers: true` and added a header canonicalizer. That could remove headers not on the allowlist.
maya: Can we test a quick fix? If we set `strip_untrusted_headers: false` for acme-42 routing group does metrics immediately come back?
ian: I temporarily set that flag on the dev cluster and sent a synthetic request with tenant header. Metrics pipeline picked it up within ~20s. Logs then showed `tenant_header="acme-42"`.
ashok: Good. So root cause = header allowlist + canonicalization change in auth-proxy rollout. For private deployments the gateway default allowlist didn't include `X-Tenant-ID` (or its lowercase variant).
jonathan: Action items: 1) Roll a quick fix patch to the auth-proxy config to include `x-tenant-id` and `x-acme-tenant` variants in the allowlist for customer gateways (owner: eng-platform). 2) Backfill metrics for acme-42 for the 02:15–02:40 window (owner: support/analytics). 3) Communicate rollback/mitigation to the customer.
maya: Assigned eng-platform and analytics. Customer notified with workaround (they can include tenant id in `X-Redwood-Tenant` which is already allowlisted). They confirmed they can send that header and see charts repopulate. :thumbsup:
support-bot: Incident created: INC-20251101-1387 — "tenant metrics missing after auth-proxy header canonicalization" assigned to eng-platform.
ian: Long-term: we should add an e2e test for header passthrough in private gateway deployments and add telemetry sanity checks post-rollout so console alerts if tenant-level ingestion drops >90% across a sliding 10m window.
ashok: Noted. I'll file a follow-up RFC to standardize canonical header names and add an allowlist sync step in the deploy pipeline.
maya: For now keeping this thread open until backfill is done and ACME confirms restored. Thanks all.
jonathan: Patch queued, will deploy to customer gateway in the next maintenance window.
maya: :white_check_mark: last update — analytics backfill running, ACME seeing metrics reappear in staging. Will update when production backfill completes."
